actions.reason: b58encode_int: drop the separate one-digit-per-divmod tail loop. The main five-digit loop now runs until the integer is zero, so the final (most significant) group is emitted zero padded like the others, and the padding is removed with a single lstrip of alphabet[0] on the joined result. The true encoding of a nonzero integer never starts with the zero digit, so the output is unchanged; for i == 0 the loop does not run and the existing default_one handling is untouched. This replaces up to four Python-level divmod iterations per call with one group iteration plus one C-level lstrip. Measured encode_ir ratio 0.9835 with equivalence output identical; decode_ir and check_ir also improve slightly (0.9943, 0.9967).
